manual.coke_and_graphite.line2: {0}Coal Coke is a purified form of carbon similar to charcoal. Coke is created from coal in the {1}Coke Oven{2}.{3}
manual.coke_and_graphite.line3: It is used in steelmaking of all forms, from the {0}simplest{1} to the {2}most advanced{3}, and is a better furnace fuel than coal.
manual.coke_and_graphite.line4: {0}Highly Ordered Pyrolytic (HOP) Graphite is a complex, allotrope of graphite used in special engineering constructs.{1}
manual.coke_and_graphite.line5: HOP Graphite Dust is created by compressing eight pieces of Coke Dust in the {0}Industrial Squeezer{1}.
manual.coke_and_graphite.line6: That dust can be then be formed into other shapes in the {0}Bottling Machine{1} as shown on the following page.
manual.coke_and_graphite.line7: {0}While graphite plates are used in assembling {1}HV Accumulators{2}, the dust can also be shaped into electrodes, essential for operating the {3}Arc Furnace{4}.{5}
manual.coke_and_graphite.line8: Both are made by placing the dust and a matching mold on the conveyor of the Bottling Machine, which packs the dust, saturates it with {0}Creosote Oil{1} and bakes it into shape.
